title: Why Are Electric Hypercars So Fast?
description:
The Rimac Nevera weighs more than two tonnes, as much as a big family SUV. It has no engine sound, no gear changes and no exhaust. And it can reach one hundred kilometres per hour in under two seconds, faster than almost any petrol supercar ever built. How? Today, ten parts of an electric hypercar, and why each one makes it so fast.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:02 1. The electric motor
2:16 2. The four motors
3:22 3. The battery floor
4:26 4. The single gear
5:35 5. The inverter
6:43 6. The power cells
7:50 7. The battery cooling
8:54 8. The flat motor
10:05 9. The tyres
11:11 10. The heavy weight
12:21 The verdict

Sources:
- Rimac Nevera: four motors, torque vectoring, H-shaped structural battery, weight, power, acceleration: Wikipedia, "Rimac Nevera" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rimac_Nevera
- Electric motor torque characteristics: Wikipedia, "Electric motor" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_motor
- Porsche Taycan two-speed transmission: Wikipedia, "Porsche Taycan" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porsche_Taycan
- Inverters and silicon carbide (Tesla Model 3): Wikipedia, "Silicon carbide" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon_carbide and "Power inverter" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_inverter
- Axial flux motors, Ferrari SF90: Wikipedia, "Axial flux motor" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axial_flux_motor and "Ferrari SF90 Stradale" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_SF90_Stradale
- Battery energy density and solid-state batteries: Wikipedia, "Solid-state battery" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid-state_battery and "Lithium-ion battery" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithium-ion_battery
- Torque vectoring: Wikipedia, "Torque vectoring" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torque_vectoring
